_comment: CLAIM multiphase::4: [API] `phi.x.array.min()` and `.max()` are RANK-LOCAL and include ghost entries. Reduce over owned DOFs only: slice to `phi.x.array[:V.dofmap.index_map.size_local]` and wrap in `comm.allreduce(..., MPI.MIN / MPI.MAX)`. Guard every print with `if comm.rank == 0:`. Signal: measured, the unguarded … WHAT THIS RUNS: `phi.x.array.min()` / `.max()` are RANK-LOCAL and include ghost entries, and an unguarded `print` emits one copy of every step line per rank. A shrinking droplet placed off centre is written into a P1 function step by step (interpolation only, so the field is bit-identical whatever the rank count) and the step line is printed exactly as an unguarded template would. Under mpirun -n 2 the run emits two copies of every step line and the two ranks report different ranges, so the printed number is not the global range. Note what is NOT reproducible: the claim says none of the per-rank ranges is the global one, but with this partition rank 0 owns both extremes and its unguarded print is accidentally right - only rank 1 is wrong. The local arrays do carry ghost entries, which the worker reports. Mutation control: T2_MUTATE=1 slices to `phi.x.array[:V.dofmap.index_map .size_local]`, reduces with comm.allreduce(..., MPI.MIN / MPI.MAX) and guards the print with `if comm.rank == 0:`; the duplication disappears and the reduced range matches the serial range exactly. OBSERVED, copied from the run: every_step_line_printed_once_per_rank=True; the_two_ranks_disagree_about_the_range=True; at_least_one_rank_misreported_the_global_range=True; local_array_carries_ghost_entries_on_every_rank=True; VERDICT=local_min_max_is_rank_local_and_prints_duplicate. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against dolfinx 0.10.0 / basix 0.10.0 (conda env `fenics`, real scalars); every expect_in_output string above is text the software actually printed. T2_MUTATE=1 runs the correct variant instead, and the fixture then fails its own expectations — checked, so it cannot pass with the pathology absent.
